[b]July 16, 2028: The Massacre at Tharkønn[/b]

John Crockery sat at his desk in the study of his four story flat, which overlooked the main square of the historic Rosenmarkket capital of Tharkønn. The city had become heavily militarized following the July 5 release of the petition, Haakon had apparently become paranoid.

Crockery had been watching for some time now the main square out of the third story window, some guards and officers had set up a watch in the square, casually milling about as passerbys hurried through the square, it was 6:30 PM.

At around 6:45 he was alerted to the window once more as the sound of drums and bullhorns filled the air, a large group of protesters had begun to march into the square, protesting the regime and the mayor who had been accused of participating in the regimes activities. It wasnt necessarily a large group, about 159 people perhaps, however, Crockery noted the soldiers tighten their grip on their guns, one of them spoke into a walkie talkie some inaudible order. A request for backup no doubt.

Within ten minutes the back up had arrived, lining themselves up on the opposite end of the square in front of the city hall, the protestors continued their jeering and taunting. It was now 7:00 PM, the clock on the city hall rang out the hour.

Suddenly, Crockery sensed a shift in the mood, leaping to the window once more he saw one of the protestors pry up a cobblestone, and with one heave, fling it at one of the soldiers, it struck him hard in the chest knocking him back as the soldiers immediately lowered their guns at the crowd, ordering them back, Crockerys stomach dropped, he knew what would happen next.

The soldiers yelled at the crowd to Get back! some protesters moved back, but a few others seemingly decided to test the soldiers, something else got thrown, a fuse got lit, something happened, then there was a scream.

At 7:15 a loud crack echoed across the square as screams filled the square, the crowd dispersed partly as the body of a college student fell to the ground, the protesters now surged at the soldiers while some quickly fled, more cracks as they met the guards, grabbing them and being bayoneted and shot.

John did not remember what he did next, grabbing his tennis shoes, he perhaps bolted down the stairs and onto the sidewalk, where horrified onlookers were already rushing into the square as the gunfire continued. John saw a body lying on the ground, blood pooling around it, it was a woman, rushing over he attempted to ascertain if she was alive, but it became clear that she was dead.

He ducked as a bullet whizzed by him, striking a parked car, the police had brought out their clubs and were beginning to beat back the protestors, one protestor had his face smashed in, crumpling to the ground with a gurgling cry.

It was 7:30 now, the crowd had begun to disperse as the soldiers stopped firing, the panicked screams echoing through the streets as the wail of the ambulances filled the air, the dying light of day casting an eerie glow over the square where soldiers walked now, inspecting the wounded and dead. 

One of the soldiers approached him, Were you with them? He asked, pointing at the crumpled body of a college student, he had fallen face down, twisted slightly.

N-no, I live there, stuttered John pointing at his house.

The soldier nodded, shouldering his rifle he nudged one of the dead with his boot, Did you see what happened,

Not really, lied John.

The soldier gave a nod, Good, he replied before walking away, shaking his head almost in disbelief himself.

John felt himself go dizzy as the stench of blood filled his nose, he moved to the curb where he sat down, civilians and paramedics rushing onto the scene, the lights of the ambulances filling the square.

He buried his face in his hands, there was no turning back now

[quote=dhornaper;61610083][b][u]The Rank of a Hundred Martyrs[/u][/b]

A few days later, the great reopening arrived. Hundreds of mullahs, clerics, and scholars arrived while the state news networks broadcasted the event over TV, radio, and the internet. President Fereydun Khan stayed aloof and detached from it. He wore a traditional langota, the Afghan choice of turban, and wrapped himself up in a shawl as he stayed seated at the front of a prepared stage outdoors in front of the renovated Khirqa Sharif Mosque. For now, he sat while Ayatollah Hossein spoke:

"I have something very important to say. We all know that the land, the water, and the air belong to Allah. So whose rules should govern Allah's country? The Elseyrians' rules? The Argosians' rules? The Kianzhous' rules?"

The gathering knew how to answer, they all rejected foreign interference. In unison, they called out

"No, Allah's rules!"

He continued.

"The Prophet said, 'If anyone is able to bring back the rules of the Quran in my name, what rank will that person then be given?'"

"The rank of one hundred martyrs!" Cried the mullahs.

The Ayatollah then announced that he wanted to give Fereydun Khan the highest title available in Islam, that of Amir al-Mu'minin, comparable to that of Pope in the Catholic church. The rules of Islam stipulated that only the Prophet himself or the ulema could grant it. Fereydun Khan had his ulema prepared. The last holder of it in Dhornaper had been the Shah, who inherited it from the time Nasrollah Shah was crowned it, over two hundred years ago.

"By making him the Amir, we are restoring our connection with the Quran, are we not? Do you too want the hundred martyrs? Do you too want the Quran restored? Will you make a pact with this Amir to achieve that? Or not?"

Again, Fereydun Khan sat there aloof while the mullahs called out in unison: "Yes, thats what we want!"

The Ayatollah concluded his speech with some words about country's leadership.

"Do you agree its time to restore the position of Amir al-Mu'minin?" He asked the audience.

Everyone answered in unison: "Yes!"

"Is His Excellency Fereydun Khan the general Amir of the Muslims?"

"Yes!"

At this point, Fereydun Khan came forward rather slowly to be congratulated by all the mullahs at the meeting, each of whom had to shake his hand, not just as a mere handshake, but as an oath to the Amir, a promise of support for as long as he lives.

After all present had swore their oath, Fereydun Khan went up to the microphone and began to speak.

"In the name of Allah..."

He was cut short. A loud whirring noise rapidly approached him. It was a makeshift kamikaze drone.

Seconds later, a loud blast rocked the platform. Fereydun Kham was thrown off the stage into seating area as his guards scrambled to shield him. He was bloodied and bruised but not badly injured. The drone had missed and hit the mosque behind him.[/quote]

[b][u][/u][/b]

[b][u]The End Of The Republic, The Rise Of The Kingdom[/u][/b]

The attempt had come close. Had the drone operator been more capable, Fereydun Khan would have been killed on live TV. As it happened, the sight of him being thrown off the stage with a cloud of smoke behind him was enough for some to begin to speculate that he had been killed anyway. It was only when he emerged from hospital after treatment, in full view of rolling cameras, that the conspiracy theories died down. He had survived and he intended to seize the moment.

The title of Amir al-Mu'minin was intended to be the stepping stone towards Shah, as the Shahs had frequently claimed it by way of inheritance from Nasrollah Shah. Fereydun Khan wanted to crown himself it and link his reign with that of the Shah's before him. The assassination attempt, however, changed things. It would not just be a stepping stone, it would be the opportunity to become Shah.

The few days he spent in hospital were used to organise a second event at the Khirqa Sharif Mosque. Invitations went out again to all scholars, clerics, and mullahs for a new event at the same mosque. They had been worked behind the scenes in those few days to approve him as Shah. They saw no reason to dispute. Meanwhile, the custodian of the mosque and its cloak, Qari Shawali, was approached and asked for permission. Even the Shahs had to make requests to his forefathers for permission to view the cloak, and he held complete permission to refuse. In any case, he, like his forefathers, would not tie themselves up in a sticky situation by refusing the ruling leader so he approved. The last time the cloak was taken out was for the announcement of the end of the monarchy and the birth of the republic, by Ayub Khan, almost a hundred years ago. The cloak had sat safely locked ever since. Fereydun Khan was aware, and he intended the flip the script. The cloak would herald in the Kingdom this time.

So, on the same day Fereydun Khan left the hospital, he had returned to the same place with a substantially buffed security detail. Snipers, guards armed with shotguns, others with rifles, all stood ready. There would be no possibility of a repeat attempt with drones.

"Here I am", Fereydun Khan told Qari Shawali. "I have taken a bath and I have put on new clothes. Let me see the robe."

They both proceeded to the shrine. The shrine's double doors were locked with three different-sized padlocks stacked atop one another like petals. Ordinarily, two of the keys are held by separate members of his family for security. Today, he had gathered all of them. Once inside, they passed under a table laden with Qurans before arriving at another set of doors, again with three locks. Finally, inside the sanctuary, the Prophet's cloak is kept inside a small silver box, which, in turn, lies inside two larger boxes.

After unlocking it, Qari Shawali took out the cloak, and handed it to Fereydun Khan. The cloak, visible only by the dim light of a few slits in the shrine's walls, moved Fereydun Khan, who was himself no more religious than most Dhora citizens. He trembled, and turned to where he thought was Mecca to pray but was corrected by Qari Shawali. After a quick prayer, he regained his composure and they both walked out of the shrine. Qari Shawali stayed behind to watch over the shrine, Fereydun Khan proceeded to the platform raised in the same place he had almost died a few days ago.

The platform was substantially higher up than before so every cleric, mullah, and scholar in attendance could view the cloak, several thousand in all, much more than last time. He made his way up the step, the cloak held out in front of him the entire way. The crowd eventually caught a glimpse of the cloak and Fereydun Khan as he approached the edge of the platform. For the next 30 minutes, he displayed the cloak openly, his palms in the sleeves as he held it in front of him. Those in attendance cheered. Some threw their turbans to try and touch the cloak, others fainted.

More importantly, the event had worked. The gathering shouted "Long live Amir al-Mu'minin! Long live Fereydun Shah!" Fereydun Khan gained the legitimacy he needed.

Fereydun Khan had become Fereydun Shah.

[quote=nordiheim;61593318][i]((Time to expand the trade a little :D[/i]

[spoiler=Modernizing an old trade agreement.]
Throughout their history Nordiheim had not often been very friendly towards monarchies and empires ruled by nobles and families claiming royal blood, as they had learned a certain amount of hostility towards them from their wars and dealings with their own overthrown nobles, this of course had also extended towards the [nation]Tranvalia[/nation] lands that would over time evolve into an empire.
While no great wars of conflicts would be made with them to create long term enmity or grudges with them Nordiheim would nonetheless refuse to do any great trade or diplomacy with them.

Nordiheims economic problems and stagnation that struck the nation in the late 50s and early 60s would start to change this fact. As the nation's counsel struggled to with economic stagnation and fighting to prevent an economic collapse, a problem that would haunt Nordiheim until the 80s they would find that they had to change their view of who they were willing to trade with which would see them opening diplomatic and trade relations with nations that was kingdoms or empires that they had not been willing to deal with before.
The Empire of Tranvalia was one of these nations as they were one of the closest and their ruling family were open to their people having many freedoms that other monarchies did not allow, though the fact that they had many farms on fertile land that produced a lot of food can also be said to have helped.

After about 2 years of negotiations, both with the Tranvalians and the people back home in Nordiheim, a trade deal was signed between the two nations in August of 1964.
This trade deal mostly focused on Nordiheim gaining the ability to buy beer, maize and grains such as wheat that they grew quite a bit of, in return Nordiheim sold them iron at preferential prices.

This brings us to the modern year of 2028 where the now 64 year old trade deal was showing its age and was desperately in need of modernizing and re-negotiation to function properly in a modern economy as difficulties were starting to properly show itself.
There was also the fact that both sides had voiced the desire for some years to increase what goods and resources that were included in it, with oil being something that the Tranvalian Empire desired to gain proper access to. Thankfully the Nordiheimians had also learned over the 6 decades that the monarchy of Tranvalia was noting like how their own nobles had been like as the common people of the empire had wide freedoms and the emperors had showed a rather clear opinion that people of merit should be given important positions rather than those of "correct birth, something that had made the whole idea to increase trade and diplomatic ties with the empire far more acceptable than it had in the past.

As such the diplomat Larsin Bindison was being sent to the Empire of Tranvalia to achieve the following goals:
-An exchange of embassies between the two nations to widen the two nations diplomatic ties.
-Widening the trade deal to a general one that allowed full trade between the two nations.
-Offer the empire access to buy Nordiheimian [b]Oil[/b] in addition to [b]Iron[/b], both at fair market prices.
-The permission for entities in both nations to make investments in the companies and economy of the other nation following each other's laws and national restrictions.
-General permission for their citizens to travel between the two nations to encourage tourism and the exchange of cultural understanding between the nations.

The council of Nordiheim hoped that Emperor Alexander Karel von Halstern I and the States General of Tranvalia would be as open to these re-negotiations and enlargement of the old agreement as they had seemed to indicate in the recent years.
[/spoiler]

[nation]Tranvalia[/nation]
[nation]Shahzada[/nation] rp[/quote]

Official Statement from the Government of Tranvalia  2028

The Government of Tranvalia acknowledges the arrival of Diplomat Larsin Bindison and the proposals put forward by the Council of Nordiheim regarding the renewal and expansion of the 1964 trade agreement.

For more than sixty years, this agreement has supported a consistent and mutually beneficial exchange of goods between our nations. While its structure no longer fully reflects modern economic conditions, its continued relevance demonstrates the value of stable and predictable cooperation.

Tranvalia considers the proposed modernization to be both timely and necessary.

Following initial review, and with the awareness of both the States General of Tranvalia and His Majesty Emperor Alexander Karel von Halstern I, the government is prepared to enter formal negotiations on the basis of the following points:

The establishment of resident embassies in each nation to ensure direct and continuous diplomatic contact.
The expansion of the current trade framework into a broader agreement allowing for increased commercial exchange across additional sectors.
The inclusion of energy exports, particularly oil, under clearly defined and reliable market arrangements.
The creation of regulated pathways for investment, enabling companies and financial entities to operate within each others economies under applicable national laws.
The controlled facilitation of travel between our nations to support tourism, commerce, and cultural exchange.

These proposals are viewed as a foundation for discussion. Final terms will be developed through negotiation, with attention to economic stability, legal clarity, and long-term reliability for both parties.

The Government of Tranvalia approaches these talks with a practical objective: to establish an updated agreement that reflects present-day realities while maintaining the consistency that has defined relations between our nations for decades.

Tranvalia remains ready to proceed.

Eleonore what is the situation? Asked Henri as he walked into the situation room of the Montfleurois royal palace, various generals and military advisers had already gathered and were watching Montfleurois and Rosenmarkket newsfeeds showing aerial views of Tharkønn and views of the shooting.

Forty three dead, sixty five injured, thats what we have as of now, replied Eleonore not taking her eyes off the screen.

F-cking hell, theyre shooting their own citizens now,  stated Henri, rubbing his forehead.

Intelligence suggests one of the protestors threw a stone at one of the soldiers, said one of military advisers.

F-cking hell, do they not have an escalation ladder? Asked Henri.

Eleonore shook her head, No idea,

Is there any word from the government yet, asked Henri.

No, as to be expected, they have remained silent, she replied.

Well we now have an ICJ case, sighed Henri.

Sh-t, he said sitting himself in the chair.

Have you a statement prepared? Asked Eleonore.

Uh yes, its rough but yes, replied Henri.

Sir, we have received word that military police have just detained the duke of Belgarde, said one of the advisers putting his phone down, From the consulate in Vierne,

We can do something because of that? Right ellie? Asked Henri, pointing at the adviser while looking at Eleonore.

I believe so, the duke is technically a foreign diplomat, even though half of his duchy is in Rosenmarkke, 

Its a breach of the act of settlement? Pressed Henri.

Id have to get the legal team on that one sir, she replied.

Alright, lets get to that, phone our representative to the International Forum, and lets call a joint legislative session, what are our military options? asked Henri, looking as some of the advisers gave him shocked looks.

Sir, that would stuttered one.

I know it would break neutrality, but one of our own nobles has just been arrested, people are being shot in the streets, now is not the time for moral grandstanding! I need options immediately, he snapped.

We have the gendarme on standby, replied one of the advisers resolutely.

Finally, clapped Henri, Someone who knows what the hell to do, come on people, and for lands sake, can someone get me a coffee and a vicodin! declared Henri as he sat down at the conference table.

With the number of protests happening in Rosenmarkket and the one that just happened in Tharkønn the Italian populace has grown restless.
